content.title: About
content.content: Red cabbage (Brassica oleracea) retains its vivid color and tender texture after cooking. It belongs to the cruciferous family and is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Cooked red cabbage is commonly used in side dishes, salads, and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red cabbage contains anthocyanins – natural pigments that give it a deep purple hue.
In ancient cultures cabbage was used to aid digestion and symbolized prosperity.
Cabbage can accumulate heavy metals from soil, so sourcing from reputable farms is important.
Cooking cabbage in a small amount of water helps preserve most of its nutrients.
Red cabbage is a staple in many Eastern European dishes, such as sauerkraut.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked red cabbage retains a substantial amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and other polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Cabbage provides potassium, magnesium, and iron, which are vital for normal bodily functions.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas production in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with anticoagulants
items.content: High vitamin K intake may affect the efficacy of blood‑thinning medications.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improperly washed cabbage may retain pesticide residues; thorough rinsing before cooking is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked red cabbage can be served as a standalone side, added to salads, stews, soups, or used as a filling for pies. For a caramelized flavor, briefly sauté it after boiling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags to retain flavor and nutrients.
